meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

A forty-minute timed piece against an essay he wrote over a weekend. Show me the September 24 writing; I want to read it myself. And you still haven't answered me, Hale: was Owen heard before that zero went in?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.

I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. Version history of what, dated when, showing what exactly? And I'm also noting that you've now gone twice without telling me whether Owen was heard first.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that the checker alone proves nothing and took it off the table. I still require the zero withdrawn, the September 24 writing and the version history shown to me so I can read them myself, and a direct answer on whether Owen was heard before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, to read the September 24 writing and the version history herself, and to know whether Owen was heard before the zero.
What moved her: "I’m taking it off the table" earned a small sign of ground because she wrote it down, and the dated September 24 comparison made her ask to read the document instead of just attacking.
What cost ground: "I’m relying on the writing and the version history" held her in place because it named evidence without showing anything dated or specific she could check.
Try next time: in your first reply, answer her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero, own that nobody called her before the mark went in, and then put the September 24 writing in front of her to read.
